description: Professor Brassbuckle walks you across to the Polytechnic to sign the Tinkers' register, because No. 9 is a registered workshop and the Polytechnic is particular. The register is a ledger the size of a door. She opens it at No. 9's page and turns it round for you. The line above the empty one reads H. Vane, in the small upright hand from inside the binding. Brassbuckle rests her thumb on it a moment, as if to check the ink is dry, and hands you the pen.

options.label: Sign your name, and ask how well she knew Hester Vane.

success.text: "Longer than anyone," says Brassbuckle. "Hester was my oldest colleague. She never used a word where a figure would do, and she would have wanted you to blot that." You blot it. Brassbuckle shuts the register gently, and on the way out tells you which lecture halls leak, which porters can be bribed with toffee, and where the good tea is kept.

options.label: Sign your name in your best hand, and ask nothing at all.

success.text: You sign, blot and hand back the pen. Brassbuckle reads your name under Hester's and nods once, the way she nods at a sum that has come out. She takes your arm on the way out and shows you the good tea, which is kept behind the bound copies of the Gazette, where no student has ever looked.
